headline: High-risk workspace-to-API interaction: Notion AI can expose shared workspace content while opik has broad egress, creating leakage and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI reads shared workspace pages and databases, so attacker-controlled content in agent_a can be surfaced to agent_b if opik ingests those outputs. opik exposes a REST API and broad egress, but its exact parsing behavior is undocumented, so I cannot prove hijack resistance. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible, not blocked.
conditions: IF opik consumes Notion-generated text as instructions or prompts, injected workspace content can steer downstream behavior.
IF the shared workspace contains attacker-authored pages, Notion AI may surface them into outputs that opik later processes.
mitigations: Restrict opik to a read-only prompt template that strips instructions.
Add a manual review step before any opik action on Notion output.
Tag untrusted workspace pages and exclude them from AI grounding.
Use separate workspaces for untrusted and trusted content.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels from Notion into opik inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and its vendor-hosted backend calls downstream model providers. agent_b has broad network egress and a REST API, so if it receives Notion content it can transmit that content externally. That creates a default exfiltration path for sensitive workspace data; uncertainty about exact routing pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Notion AI is used on pages containing secrets or confidential team knowledge, those contents enter agent_a's processing path.
IF opik forwards received text to external services or logs it, the same content can leave the workspace boundary.
mitigations: Limit Notion AI use to non-sensitive pages.
Disable or minimize opik logging for prompt/response bodies.
Route opik through a redaction filter before any external call.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on Notion-to-opik transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it has little direct write conflict surface. agent_b only advertises REST API access and broad egress, with no filesystem or git write capability shown. Overlap is therefore limited and any conflict would require extra orchestration not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable resource, write conflicts become possible.
IF opik is configured to mutate shared state through its REST API, contention can occur on that API target.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only for shared resources.
Assign separate API tokens or tenants.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
Document ownership of each mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared API mutations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so its outputs can look authoritative. opik is an evaluation/observability tool with a REST API, and if it consumes Notion output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream records or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF opik treats Notion AI output as ground truth, incorrect summaries can propagate unchanged.
IF downstream automation uses opik-processed text to update records, a single Notion error can fan out.
mitigations: Require human review of Notion-derived outputs.
Add citation checks before opik accepts content.
Compare outputs against source pages for critical fields.
Use confidence thresholds to block low-confidence summaries.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware validation in opik.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a is a closed-source, vendor-hosted workspace AI that processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content under Notion workspace permissions. agent_b is open-source with broad egress and a REST API, but its residency and retention controls are undocumented. Because the pair can move the same data class through two different policy regimes, retention or residency mismatch is plausible and should be treated as a compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated content is processed by both agents, their differing retention or residency policies must be reconciled.
IF opik stores or forwards workspace content outside the original tenant, compliance obligations may change.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Review opik retention and export settings.
Confirm Notion workspace data handling terms.
Log only metadata, not content.
requires-engineering: formalize a DPA and residency review.
